description: Defines the flat layered architecture rules, dependency constraints, generation patterns, and tag format for the unified regression suite. App-agnostic: every application resolves its own isolated suite; nothing here is specific to any application.

architecture._hierarchyNote: Numeric levels: core=0, data=1, components=1, pages=2, services=2, flows=3, journeys=4, fixtures=5, tests=6. data is a pure test-data layer (typed constants/variations) at level 1 alongside components; it imports core only and holds NO logic/locators/API calls. pages and services are peers at level 2 (UI vs API implementation). services/flows/journeys/fixtures may import data (test data flows in as parameters — never per-variant methods like createVariantAX/createVariantBX). A flow may compose BOTH a page (UI) and a service (API) — the hybrid-flow mechanism. A journey composes multiple flows (cross-feature) and contains NO pages/services/locators.

tagFormat.suite: @suite:{smoke|regression}  — a test in both suites carries both: @suite:smoke @suite:regression

test.storyAssociation: Story keys are NOT tags. They live in registry stories[] arrays (domain-index.json + catalogs), which support many-to-many (a shared test can belong to multiple stories). An optional non-functional '// story: {KEY}' comment may appear in the spec header for humans only.

fixture.exports: Playwright fixture extension with flow/journey/data and dependency injection

journey.exports: single class with one public execute() method that composes MULTIPLE flows across features (cross-feature orchestration)
journey.purpose: Cross-feature business scenario reusable across tests with different data (e.g. a multi-step end-to-end path composed from several single-domain flows). Does NOT call pages/services directly — it orchestrates flows.

flow.exports: single class with one public execute() method (single-domain business capability)
flow.hybrid: A flow may compose a UI page AND an API service to express hybrid scenarios (e.g. create via service/API, then verify via page/UI, then check backend via service). The flow controls the scenario; UI vs API is an implementation choice underneath it.

data.exports: typed test-data constants and variations (e.g. datasets keyed by variant). Pure data — no logic, no locators, no API calls.
data.purpose: Holds test data and its variations so callers pass a dataset in (e.g. flow.execute(dataset)) instead of coding one method per variant. Adding a new variation = add a data entry, not a new method.

service.exports: class exposing business API operations built on the core ApiClient (e.g. create/get/update/delete + validate-response helpers)
service.purpose: API implementation counterpart to a page. Services own HTTP request/response handling via core ApiClient; flows call service methods for the API side of a scenario. Never contains UI locators.

constraints.flatLayers: No subdirectories in any layer. tests/, journeys/, flows/, services/, pages/, components/, data/, core/ contain files directly (e.g. tests/place-order.spec.ts, data/order.data.ts). Domain is a tag, not a folder.
constraints.dataDrivenVariations: Variations (e.g. per-region/per-type datasets) live as entries in data/ and are passed into flow/service methods as parameters. NEVER create one method per variant (no createVariantAX/createVariantBX). Adding a variation = add a data entry, reuse the same capability method.

tagFormat.suite: @suite:{smoke|regression} — a test in both suites carries both tags; story keys live in registry stories[] only
